summary: Explains Local Fog Volume actors: placeable spheres of radially faded height fog layered on top of Exponential Height Fog/Sky Atmosphere, their density/falloff/albedo/emissive/sort-priority properties, use with Volumetric Fog, and tile-based culling debug cvars.
keys: Local Fog Volume Apply on Translucent
gotchas: Non-uniform scaling is not supported
No volumetric shadowing/lighting unless Volumetric Fog is enabled on Exponential Height Fog; shadows and light functions are ignored otherwise
Fog Sort Priority and the TileDebug views do not work when Volumetric Fog is enabled
Not applied to translucent meshes unless r.LocalFogVolume.ApplyOnTranslucent is 1 (default 0)

summary: Reference for the Sky Atmosphere component: project settings, planet/Rayleigh/Mie/absorption/art-direction properties, the SkyAtmosphere* material expressions for custom skydome materials, and the full list of r.SkyAtmosphere console variables.
keys: Support Sky Atmosphere Affecting Height Fog
gotchas: Planet Top at Absolute World Origin mode makes the atmosphere non-movable
Ground Albedo only matters when MultiScattering is greater than 0
Light Index on SkyAtmosphere light expressions must match the Directional Light's Atmosphere Sun Light Index
FastSkyLUT and AerialPerspectiveLUT.FastApplyOnOpaque are faster but can show artifacts with high-frequency sky detail

summary: Describes the Light Mixer editor window (Window > Light Mixer) that lists every light in the level, including light components inside Actors and Blueprints, for bulk editing, solo/mute, filtering, configurable attribute columns and user-defined Light Collections.
gotchas: Lights that are components of other Actors/Blueprints can be edited but not moved or reparented in the Light Mixer
The All collection cannot be deleted, duplicated, renamed or reordered
Added attribute columns appear in list order; column placement is not yet configurable

summary: Property reference for the Volumetric Cloud component (layer altitude, tracing distances, sample count scales), the Volumetric Advanced Material Output node for cloud materials, and the Directional Light and Sky Light cloud shadow/ambient occlusion settings.
gotchas: Cloud material must use the Volume Material Domain
Supports at most two Directional Lights (e.g. sun and moon)
Cast Shadows on Clouds is disabled for a secondary light with Atmosphere Sun Light Index 1
Multi Scattering Approximation Octave Count increases shader cost; one octave recommended

summary: Explains the default engine volumetric cloud material (m_SimpleVolumetricCloud_Inst) and its instance parameter groups: Cloud Layout textures and per-channel cloud types, Cloud Shape noise, Storm/lightning, and Multiscatter phase controls.
gotchas: Do not edit the Engine Content material directly; make Material Instances in your project's Content folder
Original UE 5.4 cloud material and textures remain in the engine folder for migration

summary: Explains combining and splitting channels in the Material Editor (AppendVector, AppendMany, ComponentMask) and the rules for arithmetic between float, float2, float3 and float4 values, including which combinations error out.
gotchas: Arithmetic between unequal vector sizes (e.g. float2 + float3) is invalid and errors; only a scalar float mixes with any size
AppendMany only accepts scalars; extra channels of vector inputs are discarded
A ComponentMask with no channels checked outputs nothing and errors downstream
Input order matters for Subtract and Divide

summary: Explains Lighting Channels (up to 3), which restrict dynamic lights to only affect actors sharing a channel, where to set them on lights and primitives, their limitations, cost and mobile support.
gotchas: Only 3 lighting channels supported
Does not work with Static lights or Static-mobility meshes; use Stationary or Movable
Only affects direct lighting on opaque materials; translucent and masked materials do not work

summary: Explains the physical units used for light intensity (lux for Directional, cd/m2 for Sky Light and emissive, candela/lumen/unitless for Point/Spot/Rect), conversion factors between them, and exposure tips for a physically based workflow.
keys: Apply Pre-Exposure before writing to the scene color
gotchas: Only Unitless is available when Inverse Squared Falloff is disabled
Image going white after placing a light usually means the auto exposure range is too limited
Switching to the extended default luminance range breaks existing exposure setups
Keep instanced/child lights on the same unit as their parent to avoid default-value propagation issues

summary: Covers CPU Lightmass baked global illumination for Static and Stationary lights: diffuse interreflection, volume lighting samples, baked AO, translucent and area shadows, Lightmass Importance Volume, and all Lightmass World Settings, light, primitive and material properties.
keys: Build > Lighting Info > Lighting StaticMesh Info
gotchas: Movable objects outside the Lightmass Importance Volume get black indirect lighting
Baked AO needs high lightmap resolution and previews poorly in Preview builds
Translucent materials do not scatter light; first bounce ignores translucent shadows; no caustics
Disabling Compress Lightmaps increases memory and disk size 4x

summary: Explains how the Indirect Lighting Cache interpolates Lightmass volume lighting samples to give baked indirect light to Movable objects and to preview unbuilt or moved static meshes.
gotchas: Samples are only placed inside the Lightmass Importance Volume and on static surfaces
Unbuilt-lighting preview works poorly for large meshes such as buildings or floors

summary: How to place Lightmass Portal actors over openings so baked Lightmass sends more rays toward Sky Light or emissive light sources, reducing splotchy noise in baked interiors.
gotchas: Too many portals drastically increase Lightmass build times
Portals are not occluded; only use them in very small levels, not open worlds

summary: Setup guide for Unreal Swarm Coordinator and Agents to distribute Lightmass lighting builds across Windows machines, including agent groups, cache, logs, CPU limits and FAQ errors.
gotchas: Windows only; Mac and Linux build lighting locally only
No GPU support for lighting builds
Requires ports 8008 and 8009
Lightmass can run out of memory on large levels with high lightmap resolution

summary: How to import externally made heightmaps and target layer weightmaps (PNG/RAW) into a Landscape, set up a basic LandscapeLayerBlend material with Layer Info objects, and match required layer resolutions.
gotchas: Heightmaps should be 16-bit single-channel grayscale; target layers 8-bit grayscale; RGB loses color and precision
Layer image must match the landscape resolution exactly or it will not import
Applying a layer-blend material turns the landscape black until Layer Info objects are assigned

summary: Guide to Landscape Paint mode: target layers, weight-blended vs non-weight-blended Layer Info objects, auto-creating layers from the material, weight blending methods, and the Paint, Smooth, Flatten and Noise tools with painting performance tips.
gotchas: Each target layer needs its own Layer Info object; reuse only works if the layer name matches
Orphaned layers (removed from material) show a ? icon and painted areas may turn black
Layer masks count toward the texture sampler limit but are not shown in stats; grey squares indicate the limit was exceeded
Final Weight Blending (Legacy) cannot override weights from edit layers underneath

summary: Reference for material parameter nodes exposed to Material Instances and runtime code: Collection Parameter, DynamicParameter for Niagara, ScalarParameter, VectorParameter, static switch/bool/component-mask parameters, and texture sample/object parameter variants.
gotchas: A material can reference at most two Material Parameter Collections; each holds up to 1024 scalar and 1024 vector parameters
Static parameters cannot change at runtime and each used combination compiles a new shader permutation
VertexColor and Transform node are mutually exclusive; VertexColor comes out white
Sampling alpha of a texture without alpha returns zero

summary: Reference for utility material nodes such as Lerp, Fresnel, DepthFade, SphereMask, Noise, Vector Noise, BumpOffset, RotateAboutAxis, Desaturation, distance field nodes, QualitySwitch/FeatureLevelSwitch, Previous Frame Switch and Thin Translucent output.
gotchas: DistanceFieldGradient and DistanceToNearestSurface require Generate Mesh Distance Fields in Project Settings
Previous Frame Switch requires Output velocities due to vertex deformation enabled
Thin Translucent needs Blend Mode Translucent, Shading Model Thin Translucent, Lighting Mode Surface ForwardShading
Vector Noise is expensive at runtime; bake to a texture once the look is set

summary: Describes the Landscape sculpt Erosion tool, which runs a thermal erosion simulation moving height from steep to lower areas with optional noise, and lists its settings.

Explains Movable (fully dynamic) lights: supported shadow methods (shadow maps, VSM, ray traced, distance field), shadow bias properties to fix acne or peter-panning, and shadow map caching for point/spot lights with its limits.
gotchas: Cost scales with number and triangle count of affected meshes and light radius
Shadow caching only for Static/Stationary primitives, not with World Position Offset materials or moving lights
Animated Tessellation or Pixel Depth Offset can produce incorrect cached shadows
Ray traced shadows need DirectX 12 with ray tracing hardware

summary: Explains Stationary lights that mix baked indirect lighting and distance field shadow maps with dynamic direct lighting, the four-overlap limit, per-object shadows for movable objects, and directional CSM/inset shadow options.
keys: Use Area Shadows for Stationary Lights
gotchas: At most four Stationary lights may overlap any geometry; extras fall back to costly whole-scene dynamic shadows (red X icon)
Lighting must be built to see their precomputed shadows
Per-object shadows need accurate bounds (Physics Asset for Skeletal Meshes, fixed bounds for particles)
Dynamic Shadow Distance Stationary Light defaults to 0 (no dynamic shadowing)

summary: Hub page for Capsule Shadows (soft character shadows from a Physics Asset capsule representation); links to the Capsule Shadows Overview and Quick Start pages.
Hub page linking lighting plugins (Day Sequence time of day, Celestial Vault, HDRI Backdrop, Sun and Sky Actor, Sun Position tool) and editor tools (Light Mixer, Environment Light Mixer).

Explains MegaLights, a stochastic ray-traced direct lighting path for many shadowed area lights: how to enable it, ray tracing vs VSM shadow methods, light complexity visualization, directional/particle light support, translucency and fog integration, scalability, profiling and limits.
gotchas: Tagged experimental; designed for ray-tracing-capable PCs and current consoles, prompts to enable Support Hardware Ray Tracing
Incompatible with the Forward Renderer; water, clouds, heterogeneous volumes and local volumetrics unsupported
Directional lights are off by default; recommended to keep the sun on deferred lighting + VSM
Alpha-masked surfaces only correct via screen traces unless EvaluateMaterialMode 1 (costly); quality drops with many overlapping lights

summary: Step-by-step tutorial building a brick material that uses the BumpOffset node (parallax mapping) driven by a height map in a texture alpha channel to offset UVs for added depth.
gotchas: Node errors until a height map is connected to Height
Too high Height Ratio causes UV swimming; tutorial lowers 0.05 to 0.005
Does not change silhouette; illusion breaks at grazing view angles

summary: How to import IES photometric profiles and assign them to Point, Spot or Rect lights via the IES Texture slot, optionally using the profile's intensity, plus performance and spot-cone clipping notes.
gotchas: With Static baked lighting results can be poor at low lightmap resolution; Stationary or Movable recommended
On Spot Lights the profile is clipped to the cone angle (max 179 degrees)

summary: Explains Directional Light light shaft settings: the occlusion method that masks fog/atmosphere in-scattering and the bloom method that radially blurs bright scene color around the sun, with GPU costs.
gotchas: Occlusion shafts can only be as strong as the fog/atmosphere
Shafts fade out as the view approaches 90 degrees from the sun
Occlusion and bloom cost separately; enable only the one needed

summary: Explains using Bent Normal maps via the Bent Normal custom output node, together with an AO map, to reduce light leaking and provide reflection/specular occlusion, and how to author them.
gotchas: Bent normal must be in the same space (tangent or world) as the normal map
Generate with Cosine Distribution and the same distance setup as the AO map; characters in T-pose
Requires an AO map connected to Ambient Occlusion
